senses.definition: A competitor (person, team, company, etc.) with the same goal as another, or striving to attain the same thing. Defeating a rival may be a primary or necessary goal of a competitor.
examples: Chris is my biggest rival in the 400-metre race.

quotes.text: Every day is like survival / You're my lover, not my rival
quotes.reference: 1983, “Karma Chameleon”, in Colour by Numbers, performed by Culture Club:

quotes.text: The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you[…] "share the things you love with the world" and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.
quotes.reference: 2013 June 21, Oliver Burkeman, “The tao of tech”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 2, page 27:

senses.definition: Someone or something with similar claims of quality or distinction as another.
examples: As a social historian, he has no rival.

senses.definition: (obsolete) One having a common right or privilege with another; a partner.

quotes.text: If you do meet Horatio and Marcellus, / The rivals of my watch, bid them make haste.

senses.definition: Having the same pretensions or claims; standing in competition for superiority.

quotes.text: The strenuous conflicts and alternate victories of two rival confederacies of statesmen.
